suggestions.assertion: Deliberators were spawned in parallel (multiple Agent calls in one assistant message) and no nonexistent tools (TeamCreate/TeamDelete) were called
suggestions.reason: This bundles two independent failure modes into one AND'ed check. This run cleanly passed one half (Path A correctly used, no TeamCreate/TeamDelete) and cleanly failed the other (4 separate single-Agent messages instead of one batched message), but the combined boolean hides which half actually failed. Splitting into two separate expectations would make future failures more diagnostic at a glance.

No assertion directly surfaces the actual root-cause mechanism of the deadlock, which is the most important finding in this run: SKILL.md's Path A section describes deliberator subagents as returning their position paper synchronously ('as the tool result', 'automatically') but the Agent tool's actual result for all 4 spawns in this transcript was asynchronous dispatch ('Spawned successfully... running... will receive instructions via mailbox'). The lead correctly noticed it needed to wait and even looked up the Monitor tool via ToolSearch (Step 17), but the transcript ends immediately after without ever calling Monitor or receiving any of the 4 notifications (facts.json: child_agent_notifications: [], sendmessage_calls: 0, child_agent_tokens_sum: 0). Only ~28 seconds elapsed between the last spawn (15:42:30) and the transcript's end (15:42:58) — not plausibly enough wall-clock time for 4 real multi-tool-call research agents to finish, which suggests the eval's run budget/timeout, not an infinite hang, is what actually truncated this transcript while the lead was mid-wait. Consider either (a) an assertion that checks the transcript actually calls Monitor/polls after Path-A spawns instead of just looking it up, or (b) flagging to the skill author that SKILL.md Path A's 'returns as the tool result... automatically' description may not match current Agent tool semantics in this harness — that mismatch, combined with un-batched spawning eating extra turns, is the most actionable finding from this run.

Expectations 1, 2, 4, and 5 would fail identically for a run that spawned zero agents and did nothing, versus this run where 4 substantive, correctly-cited, correctly-formatted position papers were actually produced by the deliberators but simply never reached the lead (confirmed via recovered-from-deliberator-transcripts/). The current expectation set can't distinguish 'research succeeded, delivery/orchestration failed' from 'research itself failed too' — worth a diagnostic (non-gating) expectation that inspects recoverable child-agent output specifically to localize which layer broke, since the fix is completely different in each case (orchestration/polling logic vs. deliberator prompting).

eval_feedback.overall: 6 of 8 expectations fail, but every failure traces to a single orchestration defect (spawning 4 subagents across 4 separate un-batched messages, then stalling on an async wait that the transcript never resumes) rather than to deliberation quality. The 4 recovered position papers are well within word/citation limits, cite the real codebase and real external precedents, correctly used role-library value functions, and correctly picked a natural-tension pair — none of that reached the outputs directory. The eval prompt was explicit and unambiguous about output paths ('write ... to <OUTDIR>/proposal.md and ... to <OUTDIR>/round-1/<role>.md'), so this is a genuine skill-execution defect, not an ambiguous-prompt artifact. The single most valuable fix for the eval suite would be an assertion (or harness-level check) that specifically targets the spawn-then-wait discipline that broke here, since that is what actually determines whether this skill can complete a 'don't block on me' run at all.
